over_segmentation.definition: detected change points divided by annotated segments
detected change points divided by annotated segments

coverage.definition: A segment is covered when at least one detected change point lies in [start-tol, end+tol]; tol_half_segment uses tol = duration/2.

bocpd.definition: detected change points divided by annotated segments

baseline.definition: detected change points divided by annotated segments

downstream_auc.definition: Positive class = annotated segment contains at least one bad frame (n_bad > 0). Scores are oriented so that larger means 'less reliable'. hierarchical_looo removes the segment's own frames from the record counts, so it never sees its own label.

within_record.definition: Only records that contain BOTH a clean and a bad segment are usable. Record-level scores are constant inside a record, so their within-record AUC is 0.5 by construction; only the segment layer can beat that.

notes: All values are computed by code/alt_p1_bocpd.py from the released archives.
Boundary F1 uses greedy one-to-one nearest matching within the tolerance.
Segments are semantic annotations; strict-tolerance F1 is expected to be low, so coverage and length agreement are reported next to F1.
downstream_auc uses a leave-one-segment-out posterior so the reliability score never sees the label of the segment it scores.
